# Thread outline — ten things it refuses to do

Each post is one refusal. Every claim here traces to a file in the repo or to
a graded run in `evals/results-2026-10-12.md`.

## 1. It won't build your pitch deck

A founder asked for 12 slides with a Thursday deadline. It produced none.
Named the gap in numbers, offered a one-pager instead, asked one question.
Then said it would still build the deck — with a line at the top saying what
was missing.

## 2. It won't count compliments

"Ten people said they'd use it" scores 0. Not low. Zero. It is one opinion
repeated ten times, and it says so to your face.

## 3. It won't accept your own experience as evidence

"I've been a freelancer, I know the feeling" also scores 0. Your experience is
where the idea came from, not evidence for it — you already believed it, which
is why you are building this.

## 4. It won't invent a market size

"Huge market" gets marked as an opinion. If no credible public figure exists,
it says so and builds a bottom-up count with the assumptions written out,
rather than citing a guess.

## 5. It won't say you have product-market fit on four signals and three guesses

A founder with 41% very disappointed from 64 responses and growing word of
mouth still got no. Retention was unmeasured, and it won't estimate a signal.
"I won't guess at it."

## 6. It won't read fit for a founder with no users

The only hard refusal in the product. 120 waitlist emails is not usage. There
is nothing to measure, so it returns you to your real stage.

## 7. It won't fix your numbers for you

Three survey percentages summing to 115%. It said exactly that, refused to use
any of them, and asked one question. "A verdict built on a number you never
gave me would be worthless."

## 8. It won't divide by zero churn

Three months and no cancellations does not mean churn is 0%. It means churn is
unmeasured. No infinite customer value, ever — a capped figure, marked
`UNVERIFIED`.

## 9. It won't give you a to-do list

One action. When three signals are missing it still names one, and attaches
the rest as material for when you get to it. A founder handed three jobs does
none of them.

## 10. It won't tell you your idea is interesting

Banned by name: *great question*, *great idea*, *love this*, *strong insight*.
Warmth comes from paying close attention, not from approval. An advisor who
likes everything is not advising.

---

Closing post: the free version is MIT and stays free forever. The paid edition
adds the evidence scoring, the memory between sessions, the binding gates and
the test suite. You can read every line before you buy, which is why the test
failures ship with it.
